text:
The patient most likely has a dysregulated reward system with low baseline dopamine tone: reduced D2 receptor availability and blunted release after chronic drug use, now in withdrawal or craving. That state would drive the agitation and the demand for medication. The team note overstates the mechanism, because most drugs (opioids, alcohol) cause functional downregulation rather than neuron death, and only methamphetamine clearly damages dopamine terminals. An acute hyperdopaminergic state, such as stimulant intoxication or psychosis, is still possible and would need a history, vitals and a tox screen to exclude.

CONFIDENCE: 55
